summary:
Pieces Left Behind is a web-based storytelling platform that brings forgotten NASA spacecraft, rovers, landers, and scientific instruments back to life for school-age space enthusiasts. Through engaging mission stories, accessible visuals, light animations, and sound, students can discover why each machine was sent into space, how it worked, and what scientific knowledge it helped humanity gain.

The platform includes a customizable content management system, allowing new mission stories to be created and published in minutes without redevelopment. Students can also interact with Astra Fox, an AI-powered guide that answers questions and encourages deeper exploration (chat bot + quiz system). Designed with a simple, student-friendly interface, Pieces Left Behind transforms complex space history into an interactive learning experience that inspires curiosity about engineering, science, and future exploration. also It has a age prefered ui system which means depends on age it will change ui theme to attract age base.
details:
What does it do and how does it work?

Pieces Left Behind is an interactive web-based storytelling platform about spacecraft, rovers, landers, probes, and scientific instruments left behind across the solar system.

Users begin with a cinematic introduction, narration, animation, and atmospheric sound. They can then explore a searchable archive of space machinery. Each story can include,

- AI Chat bot

- AI Quiz system

- Age Prefered UI system

- Mission descriptions and deployment dates

- Images, videos, and supporting media

- Narrated story segments with subtitles

- Scientists involved

- Discoveries and scientific achievements

- Interactive explanations of the machine’s purpose and technology

Users can also ask questions through Astra Fox, an AI space archive guide. Astra Fox uses the selected machinery’s information and reliable general space knowledge to answer questions in an age-appropriate and engaging way.

Benefits

The platform,

- Makes complex space history easier for students to understand

- Combines factual information with storytelling rather than presenting only technical data

- Encourages curiosity through interactive questions

- Helps students explore missions at their own pace

- Allows new mission stories to be added quickly through a customized CMS

- Supports continuous content delivery without requiring major redevelopment

- Uses narration, visuals, subtitles, and a simple interface to improve accessibility

Intended Impact

Our goal is to help school-age learners see retired or forgotten space hardware as part of an ongoing human story. The project connects engineering decisions to scientific discoveries and demonstrates how even inactive spacecraft continue to teach us about exploration, technology, and the universe.

We hope students will become interested in astronomy, physics, robotics, engineering, and future space missions.

Technologies Used

We developed the project using:

- Next.js for the frontend

- TypeScript for type-safe frontend development

- Node.js and Express for the backend API

- Supabase for database storage and authentication

- AWS S3 for media storage

- Groq’s OpenAI-compatible API for Astra Fox

- HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and responsive web technologies

- Video, audio narration, subtitles, and image assets

- Vercel for web deployment

What makes it creative?

The project presents space history as a cinematic journey instead of a traditional encyclopedia. The combination of animated scenes, narration, atmospheric audio, searchable machinery profiles, and an AI character creates a more personal relationship between students and historical spacecraft.

Astra Fox gives each learner the opportunity to ask follow-up questions, making the experience conversational and exploratory. also AI generated Quiz where student will always get random quizes generated by AI with our web machine context student referings to.

Factors Considered

Our team considered,

- The intended audience’s age and attention span

- Simple navigation and a student-friendly interface

- Accessibility through subtitles, narration, readable content, and visual storytelling

- Scientific accuracy and responsible AI responses

- The need to keep historical information expandable

- Content-management efficiency for educators and administrators

- Performance and responsive design across devices

- Safe handling of user questions and protected backend credentials

- Creating an experience that inspires curiosity rather than overwhelming users with technical details
